boundary_rationale: The scene relocates to the king's own presence: the princes report all the words, leaving the scroll behind with Elishama (web:Jer.36.20), and the king sends for it directly, וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת יְהוּדִ֗י לָקַ֨חַת֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.36.21, byte), matching “So the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll,” (web:Jer.36.21) Jehudi reads it in the hearing of the king and the assembled princes in the winter-house, a brazier burning before him (web:Jer.36.21-Jer.36.22). As the reading continues, the king himself destroys it, וַיְהִ֣י כִּקְר֣וֹא יְהוּדִ֗י שָׁלֹ֣שׁ דְּלָתוֹת֮ וְאַרְבָּעָה֒ יִֽקְרָעֶ֨הָ֙ בְּתַ֣עַר הַסֹּפֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.36.23, byte), matching “When Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut it with the penknife,” (web:Jer.36.23) A paseq falls at this same verse. Neither the king nor his servants show the expected fear or torn garments (web:Jer.36.24). Three officials attempt intercession and are refused, the full verse וְגַם֩ אֶלְנָתָ֨ן וּדְלָיָ֤הוּ וּגְמַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ הִפְגִּ֣עוּ בַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֥י שְׂרֹ֖ף אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.36.25, byte), matching “Moreover Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the scroll; but he would not listen to them.” (web:Jer.36.25) and the scene closes on the order to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah, וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת יְרַחְמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.36.26, byte), matching “The king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son,” (web:Jer.36.26) though Yahweh hides them. A fresh word-event formula opens Yahweh's own response to the burning at וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אַחֲרֵ֣י שְׂרֹ֣ף הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), matching “Then Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned” (web:Jer.36.27) -- the arrest order is as far as this unit reaches; Yahweh's reply to the burning falls outside its span.

boundary_rationale: Yahweh's own word-event formula opens the response to the burning, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אַחֲרֵ֣י שְׂרֹ֣ף הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), matching “Then Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah, after the king had burned” (web:Jer.36.27) A paseq falls at this same verse. The command to rewrite follows without a break (web:Jer.36.28), and a pronouncement naming Jehoiakim specifically opens on its own koh-amar, וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), matching “Concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, 'Yahweh says: "You” (web:Jer.36.29) charging him with burning the very scroll that warned of Babylon's coming -- a setumah falls at this same opening verse. A second koh-amar carries the sentence itself, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לּ֥וֹ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: "He will have no one to sit on David's throne.” (web:Jer.36.30) -- no heir on David's throne, his own body cast out. The punishment then extends to his offspring, his servants, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and Judah, closing on their own failure to listen (וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עָלָ֧יו וְעַל זַרְע֛וֹ וְעַל עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶת עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י עֲ֠לֵיהֶם וְעַל יֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וְאֶל אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֵ֧ת כָּל הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ (oshb:Jer.36.31, byte), matching “I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquity. I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them, but they didn't listen.” (web:Jer.36.31)); a setumah falls at this closing verse too. The chapter and the row close on Jeremiah's own replacement of the scroll, וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ אֶל בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּהוּ֮ הַסֹּפֵר֒ וַיִּכְתֹּ֤ב עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “Then Jeremiah took another scroll, and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah, who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah” (web:Jer.36.32) continuing, וְע֨וֹד נוֹסַ֧ף עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם דְּבָרִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים כָּהֵֽמָּה (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), matching “and many similar words were added to them.” (web:Jer.36.32) A further setumah closes this same verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the specific sentence against Jehoiakim (verses 29 through 31) away from the general rewrite command (verses 27 and 28) into two rows was considered, since the second half narrows to name the king specifically, but rejected because the formula וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte) and the sentence's own formula, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte), both stand inside the same divine instruction to Jeremiah, so the mouth carrying the formula stays the same across that seam.
